title: Finite Hom equation descent through the fixed monoidal squares
statement:
theorem finiteHomSiteEquationDescent
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (hdescent : ∀ n : ℕ, CoefFiniteHomDescent l E X n)
    (hsquare : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n), CoefFiniteHomSquare l E X h)
    (hmonoidal : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      CoefFiniteHomMonoidalSquare
            (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X n) (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X m)
            (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n) (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X h) (coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h)
            (finiteHomNu l E X n) (finiteHomNu l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleTensor l E X h) (coefFiniteHomProTensor l E X h)
            (finiteHomNuTensor l E X n) (finiteHomNuTensor l E X m)
            (coefFiniteHomSiteIso l E X h))
    (hquotient : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n), CoefFiniteHomQuotientCoherence l E X h) :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      (CoefFiniteHomLawsOn
            (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X n) (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X h) (finiteHomEtaleTensor l E X h)
            (finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X) →
            CoefFiniteHomLawsOn
              (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n) (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m)
              (coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h) (coefFiniteHomProTensor l E X h)
              (finiteTorConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X)) ∧
          CoefFiniteHomSuccessive l E X h

proof.text: Work directly with the recorded right tensor-Hom adjunctions. Uncurrying the evaluation-defined coefficientBaseChangeHom gives inverse tensor comparison followed by mapped evaluation. The generic scalar Hom calculus gives two-variable naturality. Naturality of the tensor comparison and the inverse-transpose identity give preservation of every transpose. Extract the intrinsic strong monoidal structure from hmonoidal; its associativity axiom identifies the two uncurried successive evaluations and proves preservation of internal composition. These equations hold on all ambient objects, hence on the specified finite-Tor constructible domain, independently of the etale-law antecedent.

Apply the existing intrinsic finite scalar tensor composition square and the generic scalarBaseChangeHom_tower evaluation calculation. This gives the required successive-quotient Hom equation on all ambient objects, including both contravariant and covariant endpoint transports. Restrict to the stated constructible pairs; the etale tower antecedent is unnecessary for this direct argument.

For the identity quotient, the ordinary restriction unit/composition comparison is the identity on sections. The derivedUnit calculation identifies the derived self-composition restriction map with restriction of its unit. Mathlib leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id therefore identifies the intrinsic self-composition associator with the unit at F(P), which equals F(unit at P) by naturality and cancellation.

Write F for self-quotient extension, mu for its fixed tensorator, and e:F≅Id for coefFiniteHomProUnit. Substitute the preceding associator identity into the tensor composition square for the self quotient. Naturality of mu at (e_X,e_Y) rewrites this as F(mu_XY followed by tensor(e_X,e_Y)) followed by mu_XY = F(e_tensor(X,Y)) followed by mu_XY. Cancel mu_XY and use faithfulness of F (it is isomorphic to Id). This proves that e is monoidal; invert its components to obtain the identity tensor equation. Apply scalarBaseChangeHom_identity to obtain exactly the required intrinsic Hom unit equation. No descent witnesses, site-Hom invertibility, or scalar-Hom invertibility are used.

proof_origin: E5: direct right-closed evaluation calculation following the final associativity/uniqueness-of-transpose paragraph of thm-coef-finite-hom.proof.md. The generic composition calculation is the same proved calculation as finiteChange_composition in the parent FiniteCoefficientHomChange, reproduced privately to avoid an import cycle. Identity normalization is deduced from the already stated self-quotient tensor composition square by cancellation and faithfulness, rather than importing the downstream CoefficientTensorNormalizationUnit.
